- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- When sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) and prices are trending down, model often underestimates; adjust upward by 1–3% to capture mean reversion.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > true by >3%), model frequently overcorrects; dampen subsequent forecast by 0.5–1.5% to avoid overshoot.
- If sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish mid-horizon, model often fails to adjust; apply a downward bias of 0.5–1.0% starting from the sentiment pivot point.
- For 30-day forecasts, model tends to overestimate early in the horizon (first 5–7 days) when sentiment is positive; apply a 0.5–1.0% downward correction to first 5 days.
- If sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67) and prices are volatile, model often fails to capture mean reversion; apply a 0.5–1.5% downward bias to mid-horizon (days 8–15) to align with true mean.
